content.title: About
content.content: Dried cherries are the dehydrated fruit of the sweet cherry tree (Prunus cerasus). They retain a characteristic sweet‑tart flavor, bright red color, and a chewy texture, while offering a longer shelf life compared to fresh cherries.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Cherries belong to the Rosaceae family and are closely related to plums, apricots, and almonds.
Dried cherries are often used as a convenient substitute for fresh fruit in baking and desserts.
The drying process concentrates anthocyanins, giving the berries their vivid color.
Historically, dried cherries have been used in folk medicine to aid digestion.
They are easier to transport and store than fresh cherries.

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: Dried cherries contain anthocyanins and vitamin C, which help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Dietary fiber in cherries promotes regular bowel movements and can help relieve constipation.

items.title: Source of potassium
items.content: Potassium assists in fluid balance and supports heart function.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Unlike many nuts, dried cherries contain virtually no fat, making them suitable for low‑fat diets.

items.title: Immune system support
items.content: Vitamin C and other phytochemicals contribute to a stronger immune response.

items.title: High natural sugar
items.content: Drying concentrates the fruit's natural sugars, so dried cherries can be calorie‑dense and may affect blood sugar levels.

items.title: Cherry allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to cherries, ranging from skin rashes to swelling.

items.title: Sulfite content
items.content: Sulfites are sometimes added to preserve color and freshness, which can cause reactions in sulfite‑sensitive people.

items.title: Dental concerns
items.content: The sticky texture can adhere to teeth and increase the risk of cavities if consumed frequently.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Dried cherries can be enjoyed as a snack, added to oatmeal, yogurt, baked goods, salads, or used in sauces and marmalades. Soaking them in water or juice softens the texture if desired.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store dried cherries in an airtight container in a cool, dry, dark place. For extended storage, keep them in the refrigerator. Discard any that develop off‑odors, discoloration, or mold.
